Title
* Please remove the space before the exclamation mark.

Goal
* Please change "certain configuration's level which gives this firewall a certain protection's degree" to "a protection level [[p]]" for consistency in terminology.

* Please add this heading above "Hackers execute":
<<Cyber attack stages>>

* Please format "ps", "bf" and "mi" as {{constants}} and remove the bold formatting currently applied to them and the brackets.

* Please replace the text from "each step" to the end of the statement with the following for clarity:

-----

There may be multiple attack attempts against the same company in a single stage.  The <<sum>> of their strengths is used to evaluate the stage. If a stage is successful, the attack proceeds to the next stage; otherwise, the attack is blocked and later stages are not evaluated.

Once the next stage begins, no further attempts of the previous stage occur.

If any stage is blocked, the company's status is {{Blocked}}. If all three stages are successful, its status is {{Hacked}}.

<<Firewall rules>>

The firewall behaves according to its protection level as follows. Each number in columns 2 to 4 is the <<exclusive>> upper bound on the total attack strength that the firewall can block.

```
Firewall       Port         Brute        Malware
protection     scanning     force        installation
level ([[p]])     ({{ps}})         ({{bf}})         ({{mi}})
------------------------------------------------------
[[p]] ≥ 7          10000        ∞            ∞
5 ≤ [[p]] ≤ 6      0            5000         3000
[[p]] < 5          0            500          1000
```

For example,
• {{10000}} means that the attack is blocked if the total strength is strictly less than 10000.
• {{0}} means that the attack is always successful (not blocked).
• {{∞}} means that the attack is always blocked.

-----

Input
* Please format all line numbers in <<bold>>. In addition, please format "n" and "a" therein as [[variables]].

* Please revise the second description as follows:

<<Next [[n]] Lines>>: A string in the format of [[name]]{{:}}[[p]] where [[name]] (string) is the company's name and [[p]] (integer) is its firewall protection level. (These lines collectively form the <<company list>>.)

* Please revise the final description similarly. In particular, "company's name" should be expanded to "attacked company's name".

Output
* Please rewrite this section as follows:

<<[[n]] Lines>>: [[name]]{{:}}[[stataus]]
where [[name]] is the company's name, and [[status]] is the status of the cyber attack on the company.
The output order is the same as the order of companies in the company list.

Constraints
* Please change 100 to 10, as [[n]] never exceeds 10.

* Please change 5000 to 100, as [[a]] never exceeds 100.

* Please specify the lower and upper bounds for the following, making sure the constraints are in the same order as the variables appear in the input:

  • length of [[name]]
  • [[p]]
  • attack strength (using the variable name)

I have a problem with the TEST "Two companies".
"Fast food" has a fire wall strength of 3. This creates the following passing conditions:
Portscan: Always
Bruteforce: Strength >= 500
Malware Installation: Strength >= 1000

Since there is no bruteforce attack with a strength of 500 or higher, a brute force attack will not succeed and therefore no malware installation can happen. This company can not be hacked with these attacks.

There is a similar problem with the TEST "Many companies many Cyberattacks".
"Mamounia hotel" has a fire wall strength of 2. This creates the following passing conditions:
Portscan: Always
Bruteforce: Strength >= 500
Malware Installation: Strength >= 1000

Since there is no malware installation attempt with a strength of 1000 or higher, a brute force attack will not succeed. This company can not be hacked with these attacks.

Can you please explain?

Mamounia Hotel in Many companies many Cyberattacks

* Please add the following constraints:

[[name]] never contains {{:}}.
All [[name]]s in the company list are unique.
There is always at least one attack of each type against every company, and the attacks for each company are always in the correct order.

Tags
* Please remove the "cybersecurity" and "Query" tags.

Difficulty
* Please change the difficulty from Medium to Easy.

Cases
* Many companies many Cyberattacks (Test 4): It seems that Blue sea's status should be "Blocked" instead of "Hacked". Please check whether my understanding is correct. If it is, please fix your code and the test case accordingly.

* Please ensure that each test case and its corresponding validator cover the same scenario. In particular, within each case pair, [[p]] should belong to the same protection-level category (high, medium, or low), and the ratio of Blocked to Hacked companies should be roughly similar.

* You're not limited to 4 pairs of cases. Please feel free to add more pairs where necessary to achieve adequate scenario coverage.

* Below is a summary of all the scenarios I can think of and how they're currently covered by the cases. ✅ means that the attack is blocked, while ❌ means that it isn't. The numbers indicate the number of companies across all tests or all validators.

  p>7 ✅ ps: tests - 2, validators - 2
  p>7 ❌ ps: tests - 0, validators - 1
  p=7 ✅ ps: tests - 2, validators - 4
  p=7 ❌ ps: tests - 1, validators - 1
  p=5/6 ✅ bf + ✅ mi: tests - 1, validators - 2
  p=5/6 ✅ bf + ❌ mi: tests - 1, validators - 0
  p=5/6 ❌ bf + ✅ mi: tests - 0, validators - 0
  p=5/6 ❌ bf + ❌ mi: tests - 3, validators - 1
  p<5 ✅ bf + ✅ mi: tests - 0, validators - 1
  p<5 ✅ bf + ❌ mi: tests - 0, validators - 0
  p<5 ❌ bf + ✅ mi: tests - 0, validators - 0
  p<5 ❌ bf + ❌ mi: tests - 8, validators - 6

  I hope I've got all the figures right. If they're correct, there are significant gaps in the current coverage *and* the balance.

* Below is a summary of how well the cumulative strength rule is covered by the cases. The numbers indicate the number of tests or validators. "inda" = individual attacks.

  p≥7 + sum has no effect: tests - 0, validators - 1
  p=5/6 + sum has no effect: tests - 1, validators - 0
  p<5 + sum has no effect: tests - 0, validators - 0
  bf:
  p<7 + inda all weak, sum weak: tests - 1, validators - 1
  p<7 + inda all weak, sum strong: tests - 1, validators - 0
  p<7 + inda all strong: tests - 0, validators - 0
  p<7 + inda weak & strong: tests - 1, validators - 1
  mi:
  p<7 + inda all weak, sum weak: tests - 0, validators - 0
  p<7 + inda all weak, sum strong: tests - 1, validators - 0
  p<7 + inda all strong: tests - 0, validators - 0
  p<7 + inda weak & strong: tests - 0, validators - 0

  Again, I hope I've got all the figures right. If they're correct, the cumulative strength rule is severely underrepresented in the current cases.

* I noticed that one or two tests contain edge cases specifically designed to check whether a solution handles the total-strength threshold correctly, but I haven't analysed how well all thresholds are covered. Please ensure that all five threshold values are covered in both of the following ways, in at least one test and one validator:

  • the threshold itself (e.g. total strength = 10000)
  • the threshold minus 1 (e.g. total strength = 9999)

• For the [[p]] = 5 or 6 category, please try to use both values for each relevant scenario.

* Please modify the cases to address all of these coverage gaps, while ensuring that each test and its corresponding validator cover the same scenarios. A single case can, of course, cover multiple scenarios.

It's getting late for me, so I'll have to review the revised version of this and your other puzzle tomorrow.

Thanks.

Just to clarify, the scenario "✅ bf + ❌ mi" should be interpreted as if bf and mi were assessed separately (i.e. mi is still assessed as usual even after bf has been blocked) for case coverage purposes. This is different from the actual rules, in which once bf has been blocked, mi is ignored.

Hi 5DN1L,

Thanks for the great feedback! 
I have applied all your formatting, text, and constraint suggestions.
I also fixed Test 4 (Blue Sea is now correctly Blocked) and updated the test cases to properly cover all threshold edge cases and scenarios as requested.
Let me know if it looks good now!

The cases definitely need more work 😅

Goal
* Please replace "If any stage is blocked, the company's status is Blocked. If all three stages are successful, its status is Hacked." with the following two paragraphs (excluding the "-----" lines):

-----

The status of the cyber attack on a company is {{Hacked}} if all three stages succeed; otherwise it is {{Blocked}}.

Cyber attack attempts on different companies may be interleaved, and they should be evaluated separately.

-----

* Please change "Each number in columns 2 to 4" to "For each stage, the value in the table".

* The table currently in the statement isn't formatted correctly. Please replace it with the one from my previous comment, starting at the first set of 3 backticks and ending at the second set of 3 backticks, inclusive.

* Please add the following paragraph at the end of the statement:

Your task is to determine the final status of the cyber attack for each company.

Input
* Next n Lines: Please remove the word "attacked" here (keep it in the other description).

* Please change "Line + 2n" to "Next Line".

* Please indicate the variable types in the final description, consistently with how they're shown in brackets in "Next n Lines".

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement.

Cases
* It seems that my previous description of how the cases should be revised may be unclear to you. To simplify this, please revise all the case pairs according to the specifications below. You may reuse existing cases where they fit the revised case set.

(continued)

Keys:
- C = Company
- aptpc = number of attacks per type per company
- ps, bf, mi = *sum* of all attacks of a stage
- ips, ibf, imi = *individual* attack of a stage

Test 1/Validator 1:
- n = 2, a = 6 (1 aptpc)
- attack order: C1 then C2
- C1: p > 7, ps < 5000
- C2: p < 5, bf > 600, mi > 1100

Test 2:
- n = 6, a = 18 (1 aptpc)
- attack order: C1, then C2, and so on, no interleaving
- C1: p = 7, ps = 9999
- C2: p = 7, ps = 10000
- C3: p = 5, bf = 4999, mi = 2999
- C4: p = 6, bf = 5000, mi = 3000
- C5: p < 5, bf = 499, mi = 999
- C6: p < 5, bf = 500, mi = 1000

Validator 2:
- Same as Test 2, but companies are reordered randomly
- Attacks should still not be interleaved

Test 3:
- n = 5, a = 30 (2 aptpc)
- attack order: C1, then C2, and so on, no interleaving
- C1: p > 7, ps > 11000
- C2: p = 6, bf < 4000, mi > 5000
- C3: p = 5, bf > 7000, mi < 2000
- C4: p < 5, bf < 200, mi > 1500
- C5: p < 5, bf > 700, mi < 500

Validator 3:
- Same as Test 3, but companies are reordered randomly
- Same scenarios but with different attack strengths
- Attacks should still not be interleaved

Test 4:
- n = 4, a = 40 (1 to 5 aptpc)
- attack order: interleaved
- C1: p = 6, bf < 5000, mi < 3000
- C2: p = 5, bf < 5000, mi > 3000 and imi < 3000
- C3: p = 6, bf > 500 and ibf < 500, mi < 3000
- C4: p = 5, bf > 500 and ibf < 500, mi > 3000 and imi < 3000

Validator 4:
- Same as Test 4, but companies are reordered randomly
- Same scenarios but with different attack strengths

Test 5:
- n = 6, a = 70 (2 to 6 aptpc)
- attack order: interleaved
- C1: p = 5, bf < 5000, mi > 3000 and imi > 3000
- C2: p > 7, ps < 10000
- C3: p = 7, ps > 10000 and [B]
- C4: p < 5, bf < 500, mi < 1000
- C5: p = 6, bf > 5000 and ibf < 5000, mi < 300
- C6: p < 5, bf < 500, mi > 1000 and [B]
- [B] means that ips or imi values should cover all three cases: > 1000, = 1000, and < 1000.

Validator 5:
- Same as Test 5, but companies are reordered randomly
- Same scenarios but with different attack strengths

Test 6:
- n = 6, a = 80 (3 to 7 aptpc)
- attack order: interleaved
- C1: p < 5, bf > 500 and [A], mi < 3000
- C2: p = 7, ps < 1000
- C3: p < 5, bf > 500 and [A], mi > 1000 and imi > 1000
- C4: p > 7, ps > 10000 and ips > 10000
- C5: p = 6, bf > 5000 and [B], mi > 3000 and [B]
- C6: p = 5, bf < 1000, mi < 500
- [A] means that ibf values should cover all three cases: > 500, = 500, and < 500.
- [B] means that ibf or imi values should cover all three cases: > 1000, = 1000, and < 1000.

Validator 6:
- Same as Test 6, but companies are reordered randomly
- Same scenarios but with different attack strengths

Thanks.

Hi, thanks for the detailed feedback!

I have implemented all of your requested changes:
- Updated the Statement and Input/Output wording exactly as requested.
- Fixed the stub generator by adding the write statement.
- Completely rewrote all Test Cases & Validators (1 to 6) to strictly match your specifications, including the interleaved attack scenarios and edge conditions.

Let me know if it looks good to go!

Thank you for making the changes.

The formatting of the statement was still incorrect, so I've updated it for you and also made a few changes to the text.

Cases
* I used C1, C2, etc. only to simplify my previous comment; I didn't expect them to be used as the company names in the cases 😆 

Please replace them with more realistic names, but avoid using real names like some of those you used previously. For example, you can use this website to generate random company names: https://randomstuffgenerator.com/random-business-name-generator . In any case, make sure that all names consist of ASCII characters only.

* Please use different names within each pair: a company name used in the test shouldn't be used in the corresponding validator, and vice versa.

* Some attack strength values appear too many times, e.g. 10 in Test 2. Please replace such values with random, distinct values of different magnitudes (ranging from 1 to 20000) across all cases.

* Test 3 and Validator 3: Please reorder the company list so that the companies appear in a different order from the attacks. The attack list itself shouldn't be reordered.

Thanks.

Same issue as well (with the Mamounia Hotel in "Many companies, many Cyberattacks". As for the "Two Companies" test, I managed to make it work but I agree that the instructions could be interpreted in a different way, which would lead to "Fast food" being blocked.

So either the instructions need to be clarified or the Test Suite needs to be corrected.

Hi Phykin, 
Thank you for highlighting this! The reason Fast food and Mamounia Hotel succeeded is that attacks of the same type against the same company are cumulative (summed together).I have updated the statement to explicitly state that attack strengths of the same type must be summed. Thank you for helping make the rules crystal clear!
